newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - UK October retail sales set to rise.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - UK October retail sales set to rise.

text.p: UK retail sales data for October, due on Wednesday, are expected to move back into positive territory on higher clothing sales and a pick-up in the housing market after a month-on-month fall in September.

The Reuters consensus forecast is for a rise of 0.5 percent month-on-month after a September fall of 0.3 percent. This would give a year-on-year rise of 4.1 percent compared with 3.5 percent in September.
"Both retail surveys and the rapid growth in personal living standards suggest that underlying retail sales growth is likely to remain strong," said David Smith, economist at Williams de Broe.

September's month-on-month fall was partly a reaction to strong spending in the summer months, when more Britons than usual spent their summer holidays in the country and a there was a sales surge inspired by the Euro 96 soccer competition.
Relatively mild September weather meant there was a weaker than usual pick-up in clothing sales as well, economists said.

"Although the trend in high street spending is still robust, the rate of growth may have slowed a little from the rapid pace seen over the summer months," said Jonathan Loynes, economist at HSBC Markets.
Strength in retail sales growth is likely in non-food sales, especially household goods, in line with the steady improvement in the housing market, said David Philpotts of Schroders.

"The cold weather we've got coming through now will be boosting footwear sales, and the recovery of the housing market will lead to continued demand for durable goods," said Ciaran Barr of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Barr added that November was likely to continue the upward trend as well.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell says overall retail sales are clearly on an upward trend and it expects a rise of 0.4 percent for October, leading to an annual rise of four percent.
"Basically the underlying trend for retail sales remains very firm...Overall I think we should look for a reasonably healthy figure, but nothing too strong," Barr said.
"I don't think there's anything too new, anything too surprising in these retail sales figures we're getting, but the risks are probably on the upside."

Economists at Schroders said the latest CBI distributive trades survey and the John Lewis sales data point to a modest expansion in retail sales in October, with a particular rebound in spending on clothing and footwear after September's drop.
